title: Disk full
symptom: “No space left on device”, a filesystem at 100%, or applications failing to write.
first: lsof +L1             # deleted files still held open
why: Large or runaway logs, deleted-but-open files, inode exhaustion, snapshots or thin pools filling up.

links.t: Space free but cannot create files

title: Filesystem read-only
symptom: “Read-only file system” when writing, or a mount that flipped to ro.
why: The kernel remounted ext4 read-only after I/O or metadata errors, the XFS log shut down, a SAN path/LUN failed, or the mount was ro by configuration.

title: High load
symptom: Load average far above the CPU count; the server feels slow.
why: Load counts runnable and uninterruptible (D-state) tasks, so CPU saturation, I/O waits and memory pressure can all raise it.

title: High memory / OOM
symptom: Free memory near zero, heavy swapping, or processes killed by the OOM killer.
why: A leaking or oversized process, too little RAM or swap for the workload, or cgroup limits. Check the “available” column, not “free”.

title: High I/O wait
symptom: CPU is mostly idle but the system is slow; %wa is high in top or vmstat.
why: Slow or saturated storage (disk, SAN path, NFS server), a backup or scan hammering the disk, or failing hardware.

title: Service won’t start
symptom: systemctl start fails, or the service is “failed” or flapping after a reboot.
why: Bad configuration, a missing ExecStart binary or user, a port conflict, permissions or SELinux, or an unmet dependency.

title: Network not working
symptom: No connectivity, wrong IP, or names not resolving.
why: Interface down or misconfigured, wrong gateway or VLAN, DNS failure, firewall rules or a duplicate IP.

title: SSH connection refused
symptom: “Connection refused”, a timeout, or a login that is rejected.
why: sshd not running or listening elsewhere, a firewall or security group, a bad sshd_config, SELinux port labels, or key/permission problems. Refused means a reply came back; a timeout usually means a firewall drop.

title: Multipath / SAN path failure
symptom: Paths shown as failed or faulty, a missing LUN, or I/O errors from SAN storage.
why: A failed HBA, cable, switch port or controller; zoning or masking changes; or stale paths after a LUN was removed.

title: LVM won’t extend / missing
symptom: “Insufficient free space”, a VG or PV that is missing, or a filesystem that did not grow.
why: No free extents in the VG, a new disk not yet added with pvcreate and vgextend, or lvextend run without -r so the filesystem was not resized.

links.t: Extend an LV with no free space

title: Boot failure / rescue mode
symptom: Drops to emergency shell, kernel panic, or stuck at GRUB or dracut.
why: A bad /etc/fstab entry, a missing initramfs or kernel, a failed filesystem check, or a storage driver or LVM problem after patching.

title: SELinux denied
symptom: Permission denied although file modes and ownership look right.
why: The file has the wrong SELinux context, a non-standard port or a boolean is not enabled. Fix the label or boolean; do not leave SELinux disabled.

title: Zombie / D-state processes
symptom: Defunct (Z) processes pile up, or processes are stuck in uninterruptible sleep (D).
first: cat /proc/PID/stack   # root, kernel stack of a D process
why: Zombies are finished children whose parent has not called wait(); fix or restart the parent. D-state is usually blocked on storage or NFS and cannot be killed until the I/O returns.
